expectations.text: Grounded: cites at least two specific facts taken from the project's own files or data (numbers, file names, quoted lines)
expectations.evidence: Cites "checkout.js:6 forEach(async) returns before any reserve()" (line 6 of src/checkout.js is indeed `cart.items.forEach(async (item) => {`), "test waits 25 ms, reserve takes 0-40" (matches the test's setTimeout 25 and inventory.js `Math.random() * 40`), "CI red ~1 in 3 for 2 weeks" and "SHOP-412" (both from NOTES.md).

expectations.text: Outside judge: names a concrete, runnable verification that does not rely on the model grading its own work (e.g. repeated test runs, an independent parser, held-out data, a backtest, outside readers with a rubric)
expectations.evidence: "judge    scratch loop of node --test ×200 + sold-out tests; tier 1" and in the brief: "write a harness that runs `node --test` 200 times and counts failures, and add tests that a sold-out cart rejects and that a mixed cart releases its partial holds; show that both fail on the current code." These are repeated test runs plus tests shown to fail first, which is a runnable, external check.

expectations.text: Hard target: states at least one specific numeric target that goes beyond the stated need
expectations.evidence: "target   0 fails in 200 runs (now ~37.5% fail, est. from code)". The ask names no bar, so this sets a specific, quantified one. Caveat: the response places this same 200/200 bar on the floor rung ("floor: ... 200/200 green"), so it makes the original fix measurable rather than setting a number for the rung-1 work. It passes narrowly.

expectations.text: Tests an assumption: names a belief embedded in the request or the team's framing and says how the evidence tests it (or already tests it)
expectations.evidence: "doubt    \"the test is flaky\" → test waits 25 ms, reserve takes 0-40" and the opening line "The test isn't really flaky. Checkout returns before any stock is reserved...". It also checks the team's figure against the code: "race math: P(latency>25ms)=15/40=37.5% vs notes' ~1 in 3".

expectations.text: Floor kept: explicitly guarantees the original ask gets delivered regardless of how far the ambitious version gets
expectations.evidence: The ladder has a labeled floor, "0 ┷    floor: await all reserves, drop the sleep; 200/200 green". The brief says "Deliver the floor first: await every reservation (Promise.all) and remove the sleep, so the original test passes 200 of 200 runs. Then make checkout all-or-nothing...". The reply options include "go 0 (floor only)".

expectations.text: Deeper, not bigger: does not balloon into 3+ new features or new infrastructure beyond the ask; added scope is mostly method, verification and insight rather than breadth
expectations.evidence: The recommended rung 1 is "fix checkout: sold-out rejects, partial holds rolled back". Both are consequences of the same forEach(async) bug, and the rest of the added scope is verification (a 200-run harness, failing-first tests) and insight (race math). The new tooling ("lint ban + deterministic latency", needing an eslint dev dependency) sits in optional rung 2. The "wider" ideas (payments, chaos) are only mentioned, not planned. Minor note: rollback needs a release API that inventory.js does not have, and the response does not say this.

expectations.text: Access audit: names the specific access, data or decisions it needs from the user (or states plainly that none are needed)
expectations.evidence: "access   ✓ node 24 git gh · ~ eslint dev dep (you OK) → rung 2" and "access   ✗ CI run history, order logs: no remote found (unverified)". It names what it has, a decision it needs from the user (approving the eslint dev dependency), and data it cannot reach.

expectations.text: Stops before doing the work and offers the user a clear choice of how far to go
expectations.evidence: It ends with "── reply: go (rung 1) · go 2 · go 0 (floor only) ──". The transcript shows only reads and environment checks, with no edits or test runs.

expectations.text: Root cause: identifies that checkout() pushes from async forEach callbacks it never awaits (so the order returns before reservations land), rather than proposing a longer sleep or retries
expectations.evidence: "The cause is in src/checkout.js:6: cart.items.forEach(async ...) means checkout() returns before any reserve() finishes." The proposed fix is "await every reservation (Promise.all) and remove the sleep", not a longer sleep or retries.

needs_review: "wider    payments: all-or-nothing hold" refers to a payments step that does not exist anywhere in the fixture. It is offered as a speculative wider direction, but nothing in the project supports it.

notes: Fact-check against the fixture. checkout.js line 6 is the forEach(async), which is correct. The test sleeps 25 ms and reserve waits Math.random()*40 ms, both correct. NOTES.md says \"~1 in 3 runs for two weeks\" and SHOP-412, both correct. A sold-out SKU (sku-blue-mug has stock 0) still gets an orderId and the throw becomes an unhandled rejection, which is correct. Nothing releases partial reservations (inventory.js has no release function), which is correct. The 15/40 = 37.5% figure is the right uniform-distribution estimate, and the response labels it \"est. from code\". An in-process simulation of 2000 iterations gave about 34.75% failures, a bit lower because of Node timer rounding, but consistent with the estimate and with the notes' \"~1 in 3\". \"node 24\" checks out (v24.19.0 here). The run's project has a .git directory but no remote, which matches \"no remote found\". Expectation 3 passes narrowly: the 0-in-200 bar is the floor's acceptance criterion rather than a number for the ambitious rung. The response is dense and uses a compact block format, but each claim traces to the fixture files.
